title: The postcard run, iii
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: A postcard of Lisbon. The writing says Barcelona. The strip redraws the manic handwriting and the wrong city and lets them disagree.

panels.composition: The bedroom. WOOD with a postcard. BARNABY. The picture side: LISBOA, a tram, a hill.

image.prompt: brush-pen over blue pencil, xerox grain, stark black spotting, a young man on a bed holding a postcard of a Lisbon tram on a hill, a dog beside him

panels.composition: The writing side, redrawn in the strip's version of her hand — slanting, crowded, words climbing the stamp: 'Barcelona is loud. I'm loud in it. Nobody here knows what a grunion is. I told them. —C.'

image.prompt: brush-pen over blue pencil, xerox grain, stark black spotting, close-up of a postcard's writing side crowded with slanting manic handwriting that climbs up around the stamp
image.notes: Letter after. The text is redrawn in Chloe's hand, not the strip's lettering.

panels.composition: Wood turning it over. Lisbon. Over. Barcelona. Over. Lisbon.

image.prompt: brush-pen over blue pencil, xerox grain, stark black spotting, a young man flipping a postcard back and forth between its picture side and its writing side

panels.composition: The postcard pinned by one corner beside the others, spinning slightly. Both cities. The dog watching it spin. Wood's reply: not shown. His pen, capped, in the foreground.

image.prompt: brush-pen over blue pencil, xerox grain, stark black spotting, a postcard pinned by one corner to a wall beside three others and turning slightly, a dog watching it, a capped pen in the foreground, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; xerox; black and white

notes: Lisbon on one side, Barcelona on the other. The reply is a capped pen.
